newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-CHAUHAN SOON MAKES HIS MARK IN TOUR OPENER.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CHAUHAN SOON MAKES HIS MARK IN TOUR OPENER.

text.p: Off-spinner Rajesh Chauhan, given a chance to resurrect his career after his bowling action was questioned, took two wickets in India's opening tour match on Wednesday.
Chauhan removed both openers as the Sri Lanka Board President's XI made 233 for six, in reply to India's first innings of 308, at the close on the second day of the three-day match.
His action, questioned by the International Cricket Council (ICC), the sport's governing body, has been under a cloud since his country's 1995 home test series against New Zealand.

In May, a Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) panel made up of two former India captains, Kapil Dev and Sunil Gavaskar, investigated the charge of throwing and found that video footage of Chauhan in action was inconclusive.
He was subsequently chosen for the tour of Sri Lanka, and ended his first bowling stint with two for 58 from 29 overs.
India, having added 13 to their overnight 295 for nine, were held up by an opening stand of 134 between Russell Arnold and Chaminda Mendis.
Then Chauhan and left-arm spinner Nilesh Kulkarni, who captured three for 78, checked the local team's progress.
Chauhan struck with his first delivery after tea, having Arnold caught at slip by captain Sachin Tendulkar for a well-compiled 65.
The left-hander had made full use of a dropped catch at 16 by Tendulkar off Chauhan to hit 11 fours in his 216-minute innings.

Chauhan also had Mendis caught by Navjot Sidhu at long-on in his next over for 55. Mendis too had benefited from a Tendulkar lapse when he failed to hold on to an edge at seven, and the batsman went on to hit nine fours in a stay of 224 minutes.
Once the breakthrough was achieved, the Indian bowlers made inroads into the middle order.
India's first innings was wrapped up after 14 minutes in the morning, leg-spinner Upul Chandana finishing with his best figures in a representative match of five for 86.
